merger_name: Impression Dental Group – Kingston Beach Dental, TAS

targets.name: KINGSTON BEACH DENTAL PROFESSIONALS PTY LTD

merger_description:
General Dental Holdings Pty Ltd (trading as Impression Dental Group) (**IDG**) proposes to acquire 100% of the assets of the dental practice known as Kingston Beach Dental through a business sale and purchase deed.

Kingston Beach Dental is owned by Dr Martyn Sweet and Felicity Sweet through Kingston Beach Dental Professionals Pty Ltd and supplies general dental services from its clinic in Kingston, a town on the southern outskirts of Hobart, TAS.

IDG is an Australian-based dental support organisation that provides centralised services including recruitment, payroll, marketing, IT, finance, and operations, to enable dental practitioners to focus on providing dental services. IDG currently owns and supports 23 independently branded dental practices in Australia which provide dental services to the public, but IDG does not have any practices in Tasmania.

IDG is controlled by Genesis Capital (**Genesis**), an Australian-based private equity firm that invests in businesses operating in the healthcare sector.

Genesis Capital’s investments also include Pacific Smiles Group (**PSG**) which sets up new dental centres from which dentists run their practice and provides operational support. PSG has over 120 dental centres across Australia, but has no clinics in Tasmania. PSG’s dental centres are typically conveniently located inside shopping centres and operate under the Pacific Smiles Dental and nib Dental Care brands on the East Coast.

determination_table_content.details:
General Dental Holdings Pty Ltd, trading as Impression Dental Group
(IDG), applied for a notification waiver in respect of its proposed
acquisition of 100% of the assets of the dental practice known as
Kingston Beach Dental, as described in the transaction documents
provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, IDG, is an Australian-based dental support organisation
that provides centralised services including recruitment, payroll,
marketing, IT, finance, and operations, to enable dental practitioners
to focus on providing dental services. IDG currently owns and
supports 23 independently branded dental practices in Australia
which provide dental services to the public. IDG does not have any
dental practices in Tasmania.
IDG is controlled by Genesis Capital (Genesis), an Australian-based
private equity firm that invests in businesses operating in the
healthcare sector. Genesis Capital’s investments also include Pacific
Smiles Group (PSG) which sets up new dental centres from which
dentists run their practice and provides operational support. PSG has
over 120 dental centres across Australia, but has no clinics in
Tasmania. PSG’s dental centres are typically located inside shopping
centres and operate under the Pacific Smiles Dental and nib Dental
Care brands on the East Coast.
The target, Kingston Beach Dental, is owned by Dr Martyn Sweet and
Felicity Sweet through Kingston Beach Dental Professionals Pty Ltd
and supplies general dental services from its clinic in Kingston, a
town on the southern outskirts of Hobart, TAS.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. There is no horizontal overlap between IDG (including
its connected entities such as PSG) and Kingston Beach Dental in
the supply of dental services in the local area surrounding Kingston
Beach Dental, nor in Tasmania.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
